item.title: Anthropic's Claude AI Discovers New Enzyme System in DNA Sequences
item.description:
Anthropic’s Claude AI Discovers New Enzyme System in DNA Sequences

Anthropic has announced that its AI, Claude, has autonomously discovered a new enzyme system similar to the machinery used in the gene-editing tool Crispr.

⚙️ Key details

  • Discovery: A previously uncharacterized enzyme system found in bacteriophages (viruses that infect bacteria).
  • Resources used: Nearly 1,000 Claude agents processed 210 million tokens over a period of 21 hours.
  • Method: Claude searched through a massive database of DNA sequences until one agent identified and flagged an unusual repeating pattern for human review.
  • Human involvement: Anthropic scientists were limited to the initial prompt and the subsequent lab work.

💡 Why it matters

This discovery is the first result from Anthropic’s newly-launched wet lab and serves as an early test of Claude’s usefulness for science as the company prepares to go public. While Anthropic is still working to understand the function of the enzyme system, the company stated it was important to share the findings early to demonstrate Claude’s capabilities and provide the community with insight into their work.

#Anthropic #Claude #AI #Biotechnology #Enzymes

Source: Anthropic’s biolab made a discovery it’s comparing to Crispr

item.title: FDA Approves Reduced Monitoring Time for Amgen IMDELLTRA Lung Cancer Treatment
item.description:
FDA Approves Reduced Monitoring Time for Amgen IMDELLTRA Lung Cancer Treatment

Amgen has announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved an update to the prescribing information for IMDELLTRA (tarlatamab-dlle). The update significantly reduces the recommended monitoring period for the first two doses of treatment for patients with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC).

⚙️ Key details

The new approval shortens the required monitoring time for patients receiving their initial infusions of IMDELLTRA in an appropriate healthcare setting. This change is based on an evolution in the administration of the therapy and reinforced by Amgen’s commitment to addressing real-world patient needs.

  • Monitoring Period Update: Patients are now monitored for 6 to 8 hours from the start of the first two infusions, a reduction from the previously recommended 22 to 24 hours.
  • Follow-up Assessment: Patients must receive an assessment, including vital signs, the day after each of the first two doses (Cycle 1, Days 2 and 9).
  • Proximity Requirements: For the first two doses, it is recommended that patients remain within one hour of an appropriate healthcare setting for a total of 48 hours from the start of infusion, accompanied by a caregiver.
Treatment Phase Monitoring Duration Requirement
First Two Doses (Cycle 1, Days 1 & 8) 6-8 hours
Third Dose (Cycle 1, Day 15) and Cycle 2 6-8 hours
Cycles 3-4 3-4 hours
Cycle 5 and Subsequent Doses 2 hours

🧩 How it works

IMDELLTRA is a first-in-class targeted immunotherapy indicated for adult patients with ES-SCLC whose disease has progressed on or after platinum-based chemotherapy.

  • Molecular Binding: The therapy is engineered to bind to both DLL3 on tumor cells and CD3 on T cells.
  • Immune Activation: This dual-binding activates T cells to kill DLL3-expressing SCLC cells by forming a cytolytic synapse, resulting in the lysis of the cancer cell.
  • Target Specificity: DLL3 is a protein expressed on the surface of SCLC cells in approximately 85-96% of patients, but it is minimally expressed on healthy cells.

💡 Why it matters

Small cell lung cancer is an aggressive form of cancer where most patients experience disease progression after first-line treatment. Jay Bradner, M.D., executive vice president, Research and Development, Artificial Intelligence and Data at Amgen, noted that the time required for treatment and monitoring can add to the burden for both patients and care centers.

Reducing monitoring to 6-8 hours for initial doses addresses practical barriers, particularly for the 80% to 85% of U.S. cancer patients who receive care at community oncology practices. David M. Waterhouse, MD, MPH, FASCO, a medical oncologist at Oncology Hematology Care, stated that reducing the monitoring period makes the treatment more feasible for community practices, allowing patients to receive care closer to home and their support systems.

To manage risks such as cytokine release syndrome (CRS), IMDELLTRA is initiated using a step-up dosing schedule. Ongoing studies continue to evaluate reduced post-infusion monitoring across different indications and lines of therapy to inform future approaches.

#Oncology #Biotech #FDA #Immunotherapy #LungCancer

Source: FDA APPROVES REDUCED MONITORING TIME FOR FIRST TWO DOSES OF IMDELLTRA®

item.title: NVIDIA Introduces BioNeMo Inference Runtime for Biomolecular Structure Prediction
item.description:
NVIDIA Introduces BioNeMo Inference Runtime for Biomolecular Structure Prediction

NVIDIA has introduced the BioNeMo Inference Runtime (BioIR), designed to accelerate supported biomolecular structure-prediction models on NVIDIA GPUs while maintaining a PyTorch workflow.

🔍 Overview

BioIR speeds up model execution using optimized kernels and, where applicable, CUDA Graphs. It supports an end-to-end processor that moves an InputRequest through the following stages:

  • Parsing
  • Tokenization
  • Feature generation
  • GPU inference
  • PDB or mmCIF writing

🧩 How it works

BioIR offers two executor backends for the end-to-end processor workflow:

Backend Functionality
Serial Runs each stage in sequence for one input, completing the full workflow before moving to the next input.
Ray Runs a complete model replica on each GPU in a single node to increase overall throughput for large batches of independent inputs.

Direct PyTorch integration allows users to construct a supported model (torch.nn.Module) or reuse selected modules in custom code.

⚙️ Key details

System Requirements:

  • Python 3.12 or later
  • A compatible NVIDIA GPU and driver
  • A BioIR wheel or supported development environment
  • A staged model checkpoint (such as Boltz-2) and required chemical metadata

Technical Specifications:

  • Input Requirements: Each protein chain requires an A3M MSA. For inputs with multiple non-identical protein chains, paired or unpaired MSAs are accepted.
  • Deployment: The wheel contains precompiled CUBINs, removing the need for nvcc, CUDA source, CMake, or the CUDA toolkit during runtime use.
  • Capabilities: The end-to-end processor supports ligand structure prediction, though it does not support ligand-affinity prediction. Because BioIR does not run HHsearch or HMMsearch, users can optionally supply their own templates.
  • Measurement: model_inference_time is the CUDA-synchronized folding-model forward measurement, which excludes parsing, tokenization, feature generation, postprocessing, and writing.

💡 Why it matters

BioIR has been utilized in real proteome-scale work, including the expansion of the AlphaFold Database (AFDB). This accelerated the generation of protein-complex structures across 4,777 proteomes, totaling about 31 million candidate complexes, with 1.81 million released as high-confidence predictions.

#NVIDIA #BioNeMo #BioIR #Proteomics #PyTorch

Source: High-Throughput Structure Prediction with BioNeMo Inference Runtime | NVIDIA Technical Blog

item.title: 🧬 AI Agents Transforming Life Sciences: How Data is Powering the Next Healthcare Revolution
item.description:
🧬 AI Agents Transforming Life Sciences: How Data is Powering the Next Healthcare Revolution

𝗦𝘂𝗺𝗺𝗮𝗿𝘆: At the 7th Annual AWS Life Sciences Symposium, industry leaders revealed how generative and agentic AI are revolutionizing healthcare innovation. This article explores how leading companies are unifying data silos, deploying real-world evidence, and implementing AI agents that accomplish in minutes what previously took days—while highlighting practical tools any organization can leverage today.

🔬 The AI Revolution in Life Sciences Has Arrived

When over 1,000 life sciences industry leaders converge to discuss technology’s future, patterns emerge. At the recent AWS Life Sciences Symposium in New York City, one message resonated across all 26 sessions: generative AI has moved beyond experimentation into delivering tangible results, with the life sciences sector leading this transformation.

The symposium revealed a pivotal shift—organizations are no longer pursuing AI initiatives for innovation’s sake. Instead, they’re strategically scaling proven solutions that deliver measurable outcomes in research, clinical trials, manufacturing, and commercial operations.

But what’s the secret ingredient behind successful AI implementation? The answer was unanimous: 𝙙𝙖𝙩𝙖.

📊 Data as the Ultimate Differentiator

“Your AI is only as smart—and as strategic—as the data behind it.”

This statement encapsulates perhaps the most critical insight from the symposium. Companies achieving breakthroughs aren’t necessarily those with the most sophisticated AI algorithms, but rather those who’ve successfully transformed fragmented data into unified strategic assets.

AWS categorizes this data into three critical buckets:

  • Your existing data
  • New data you create
  • Third-party data

The symposium showcased how Merck Research Labs exemplifies this approach. Their team created a clinical data layer on AWS that consolidates clinical and operational information across studies onto a single platform, enabling automation that dramatically accelerates processes.

Another game-changing element is real-world data (RWD). Consider this striking statistic: 85% of FDA drug approvals between 2019-2021 leveraged real-world evidence. Despite its proven value, working with RWD has historically been slow and frustrating—taking up to four months to process. AWS partnerships have reduced this timeline to as little as two weeks.

📸 Imagine a data pipeline visualization showing the transformation from months-long processes to weeks

The collaboration between AWS, the Broad Institute, and Manifold AI further illustrates this data revolution. This partnership combines seamless data access with advanced analysis capabilities using AWS HealthOmics, Amazon Bedrock, and Anthropic’s Claude to power AI-driven research at unprecedented scales.

🤖 From Experiments to Excellence: Scaling What Works

A clear trend emerged from the symposium: forward-thinking organizations have moved beyond random AI experiments to strategically scaling successful use cases.

Johnson & Johnson’s approach exemplifies this shift. The company has pivoted to focus exclusively on their highest-value AI applications—a strategy that enables faster ROI, better resource allocation, and sustainable innovation.

Sanofi provided another compelling case study. Their AI-powered assistant “Concierge” delivers contextual answers about company policies and procedures. The impressive adoption rate—over 80% of Sanofi employees—demonstrates how deeply AI can integrate when it solves genuine daily challenges.

The most successful implementations target specific high-impact challenges. Working with PwC, AWS identified several use cases delivering significant value:

  • 🔍 Biomarker Discovery: AI agents mining literature and first-party data
  • 📋 Regulatory Amendment Analysis: Reducing costly protocol amendments through AI-powered feedback analysis
  • 🧪 Clinical Trial Analysis: AI-guided exploration accelerating insights
  • 🏭 Manufacturing Execution System Chat: Natural language interfaces extracting actionable intelligence
  • 💼 Sales Concierge: Supporting commercial teams with timely, relevant data
  • 🔐 Fraud Detection: AI-driven anomaly detection in drug pricing programs
  • 📈 Protocol Generation: Accelerating clinical trial design through AI-assisted drafting

To facilitate adoption, AWS has created the Life Sciences Generative AI Portal—a curated collection of over 40 generative AI demos and customizable prototypes already delivering value across R&D, clinical development, manufacturing, and commercial operations.

🧠 The Next Frontier: Agentic AI in Action

Perhaps the most exciting developments centered around 𝙖𝙜𝙚𝙣𝙩𝙞𝙘 𝘼𝙄—AI systems that can independently perform complex sequences of tasks to achieve specific goals.

Genentech showcased this potential with a striking example: A distinguished scientist completed a complex analysis of cell surface receptors in just 10 minutes using agentic AI—a task that previously required two full days of work.

To accelerate adoption across the industry, AWS recently introduced an open-source agentic AI toolkit built on Amazon Bedrock. This toolkit includes:

  • Research Agents: For target identification, biomarker discovery, and experimental design
  • Clinical Agents: Supporting trial analysis, protocol optimization, and patient stratification
  • Commercial Agents: Generating competitive intelligence and market insights

📸 Conceptual illustration of multiple AI agents working together to solve complex research problems

Publisher Wiley collaborated on an agent capable of searching full-text articles published under creative commons licenses. This agent delivers reliable, cited insights in minutes rather than the hours or days typically required for literature review—a transformational time-saving tool for researchers.

The toolkit’s architecture allows individual agents to connect with multi-agent supervisors using Amazon Bedrock’s collaboration capabilities, enabling developers to orchestrate across agents and build sophisticated workflows.

🚀 Building on a Foundation for Future Innovation

The symposium made clear that while technology continues advancing at breakneck speed, success depends on establishing a scalable, secure data foundation. This foundation enables organizations to adapt and evolve regardless of what innovations emerge next.

The life sciences industry stands at an inflection point where AI is transitioning from experimental to essential. Organizations that unify their data, implement strategic AI use cases, and embrace agentic capabilities are positioned to lead the next wave of healthcare breakthroughs.

What will your organization’s AI strategy prioritize in this rapidly evolving landscape? Will you focus on data integration, specific use case implementation, or exploring agentic capabilities?
